tracks.narration: A disk read takes millions of CPU cycles. While the disk works, what should the processor do?
Polling means the CPU asks the device, again and again — is it ready yet? Every check is a wasted cycle, and almost every check returns no.
Interrupts flip the question around. The CPU issues the request, runs something else, and the device fires an interrupt when it is done.
Stack the two side by side. With polling the CPU's wait is wasted. With interrupts that same time becomes throughput for the rest of the system.
Interrupts give you concurrency for free. Polling only makes sense when the wait is so short an interrupt would cost more than the wait itself.
